close_reason: Added QueryResult::new_clamped(position_signed: i64, ...) constructor that clamps negative request-side offsets to u64. Plain new() kept for backends that have a u64 already. Bead's debug_assert option was rejected (heuristic, not a real safety net); contract test option deferred.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:609-628 — QueryResult.position is
typed as u64 with the doc:

> RFC 8620 §5.5 specifies this as `UnsignedInt` in the response —
> a non-negative integer (bd:JMAP-wlip.25). The request-side
> position parameter accepts negative values as end-relative
> offsets, but the response position cannot validly be negative.
> Backends that derive `position` from a request-side `i64`
> offset MUST clamp / normalize to `u64` before constructing this
> struct.

The corresponding backend method takes `position: i64` (backend.rs:878):

    fn query_objects<O: ...>(..., position: i64) -> ...;

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That the returned QueryResult::position is correct relative to
   the request-side i64 offset semantics. A backend that does:
       QueryResult::new(ids, 0, total, state, true)
   for a `position: -5` request when the result set has fewer than
   5 items has produced a misleading response: per RFC 8620 §5.5,
   the response position should equal the actual offset of the
   first returned id, which for an end-relative request with no
   valid offset is implementation-defined but conventionally 0.

2. That the kit catches malformed positions. QueryResult::new is
   total — accepts any u64. No assertion in the constructor, no
   debug_assert, no wrapping that the response makes sense against
   the (filter, limit, position) tuple from the request.

3. That the asymmetry between i64 request input and u64 response
   output is checked anywhere. Backends with bugs ship malformed
   responses; downstream queryChanges then operates on a
   queryState that drifted from the actual server state.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- A backend implementor reads the i64 request param doc, derives a
  signed offset, returns the i64 verbatim cast to u64 via `as u64`
  → silent wraparound for negative values, malformed wire response.
- A backend implementor reads the request as u64 (ignoring the
  i64 negative-offset semantics), and the position field in their
  response represents the wrong thing entirely (off by the
  signed-negative offset's magnitude).
- A wire-conformance test against a known-correct server (e.g.
  jmap-test-suite) catches the bug at the integration layer,
  hundreds of test runs after the bug landed.

Resolution paths:

- Introduce `QueryResult::new_clamped(ids, position_signed: i64,
  total_len: u64, total, state, can_calc)` that does the clamp
  inside the constructor with documented semantics.
  Backend impls call this when they have an i64 offset; the
  existing `new` stays for backends with a u64 offset already.

- Add a debug_assert in QueryResult::new that the position is
  reasonable relative to ids.len() — e.g. position > 1_000_000
  with ids.len() = 5 trips a warning. Heuristic but cheap.

- Strengthen the doc on QueryResult.position to include an
  example showing the clamp arithmetic.

- Add a contract test in jmap-server's own test suite that
  feeds a synthetic backend with an out-of-range position and
  asserts the response shape is what the spec demands.

This is the canonical pattern of "request type is i64, response
type is u64, the contract on the backend implementor is in a doc
comment". The doc is correct; the type-level safety net is missing.
title: QueryResult::position contract requires backend self-clamp but type accepts unchecked u64
